tweets: An external contract can seize control flow and call back before your function finishes.
This allows a malicious caller to re-enter your code mid-execution.
The root cause is updating state after the external call, relying on stale data.
Remediation: perform all internal state changes before making any external calls.
This ordering pattern is known as Checks-Effects-Interactions.
A reentrancy lock blocks unwanted callbacks but does not stop control passing to the callee.
Compiler and EVM versions may affect how these behaviors manifest in practice.
